what_happened: Job 20261102-161126-hn31 ("Refuse readings that join a full timed test run with a fix") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the plan's references real and its gate placement, corpus mechanism, brief and CHANGELOG work sound. One major finding remained: the plan's fix signal counts any `.rs` deliverable as "a fix chosen from the result". That makes the refusal also hit a legitimate speed-up fix stage that checks its result by timing the full run in one clause. That is the very stage the error message tells readers to write. None of the plan's accept cases covers it. Two minor findings: the object-word allow-list misses article-less imperatives, and the scanned set is every bullet line with its "- " marker, not only acceptance bullets. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The plan for a new reading-refusal rule designed its detector (fix signal, verb and object-word matching, scanned lines) from the reading's wording. It was not run against real past request shapes or against the compliant follow-up the refusal itself recommends. Planning has no step that replays a proposed rule over a corpus of accepted and refused readings, so false-refusal and coverage gaps show up only when the critic reasons about them, and by round 3 that loses all planning spend. Planning keeps no partial plan, and it has no repair step for a gap that reading the code and past requests would settle. The code does already know how requests are laid out (request_text_acceptance returns every bullet), but the plan did not use that.
prevention: Require every plan for a new refusal or matching rule to include accept and refuse cases drawn from real past readings and requests. Include the compliant shape the refusal message recommends (a fix stage that checks its speed-up by timing the full run). A code check should run the planned detector over a corpus of stored real readings before the plan is accepted, and should list which previously accepted readings would now be refused. The plan must also state the exact scanned lines (bullet markers, article-less imperatives) and settle them by reading the parser code instead of leaving them as open questions.
proposed_request: Re-ask job 20261102-161126-hn31: make the reading stage refuse a reading that joins a full timed test run (measuring the whole suite's timings) with the fix chosen from that result in the same job. The measurement and the fix must be separate jobs, with the fix depending on the measurement job. Acceptance: (1) a reading whose acceptance bullets both run the full timed suite and fix the biggest cause is refused, with an error that says to split it into a measure job and a fix job. (2) A fix-stage reading that cites already recorded timings and checks its speed-up by timing the full run in one clause is accepted. A reading with a `.rs` deliverable alone is not treated as the fix signal. (3) Article-less imperatives such as "Run full test suite and time it" are caught. (4) The scan uses only the acceptance bullets of the request, with the '- ' marker stripped. (5) The new check has a refusal corpus case for each of (1)-(4), including accept cases from real past readings, and each case fails without the check. (6) A reader rule line in the reading brief stays within the existing rule count and size test. (7) A CHANGELOG entry is added. The deliverables are reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, briefs.rs and CHANGELOG.
